subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Strangler Fig Pattern
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Strangler Fig Pattern usable.

hook.text: A strangler fig tree grows around its host, slowly replacing it. That's how you migrate from a monolith.

buildup.text: Instead of rewriting everything at once, you build new services alongside the old system and route traffic gradually.

discovery.text: Feature by feature, the new system takes over. The old monolith shrinks until it can be safely removed.

twist.text: Many teams get stuck in the middle: running both old and new systems for years, paying double the cost.

climax.text: The strangler fig pattern is the safest migration path. Risky big-bang rewrites fail far more often.

punchline.text: Don't rewrite everything at once. Strangle the old system slowly.

quiz.question: What is the strangler fig pattern?
options: Gradually replacing a monolith by building new services alongside it
Shutting down the old system and launching a complete rewrite
Running two identical copies of the same system for redundancy

details.summary: The strangler fig pattern incrementally replaces a legacy system by routing specific features to new services while the old system continues handling everything else. Over time the new system grows until the legacy system can be decommissioned entirely.
details.whyItMatters: Big-bang rewrites are risky and often fail. The strangler fig enables safe, gradual modernization with continuous delivery of value and reduced risk at each step.
takeaways: Legacy functionality is replaced incrementally, not all at once
A routing layer directs traffic to old or new implementation
Risk is minimized because rollback is always possible

faq.question: Where does the name strangler fig come from?
faq.answer: It refers to strangler fig trees that grow around a host tree, gradually replacing it. Martin Fowler coined the pattern name. The new system wraps around the old one, taking over functionality piece by piece until the original is no longer needed.

faq.question: How do you implement the routing layer?
faq.answer: An API gateway or reverse proxy inspects incoming requests and routes them to either the legacy system or the new service based on URL path, feature flags, or user segments. This layer is the key to incremental cutover and safe rollback.
